description: This model, by Marcella Martins, Ricardo Lueders and Myriam Delgado of the Federal University of Technology Parana (UTFPR) in Curitiba, is a discrete event simulation for scheduling operations in a complex of one harbour and two refineries linked by a pipeline infrastructure. It was presented at the Rio Pipeline 2009 conference in Rio de Janeiro and is indexed in ETDE Web. Built in the Arena package, it has three sub-models that control pier allocation, the loading of tanks and the transfers to the refineries through the pipelines. Preliminary results for one control policy show that profit can be calculated from parameters such as the cost of oil held on ships, pier use, ship over-stay and interface costs between products. Coverage: a single Brazilian harbour-refinery system, not named in the abstract. Access: the ETDE record gives the abstract and bibliographic data; the 8-page paper is not online there and the model files were not released. Licence and cost: the record states that commercial reproduction is prohibited; the paper and model are on request. Caveats: preliminary results only, one control policy and no stated validation. It shows how discrete-event simulation supports capacity planning and optimisation of pipeline and port scheduling in oil supply chains. It relates to the pipeline agent decision support model and the MiniPortSim container terminal simulator in the catalogue.
